payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanisms+of+path+dependence+and+divergent+value+evolution+in+reinforcement+learning+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6357078\", \"title\": [\"Anticipatory Reinforcement Learning: From Generative Path-Laws to Distributional Value Functions\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper introduces Anticipatory Reinforcement Learning, a novel framework designed to bridge the gap between non-Markovian decision processes and classical reinforcement learning architectures. In environments characterised by jump-diffusions and structural breaks, traditional state-based methods often fail to capture the essential path-dependent geometry required for accurate foresight. We resolve this by lifting the state space into a signatureaugmented manifold, where the history of the process is embedded as a dynamical coordinate. By utilising a selfconsistent field approach, the agent maintains an anticipated proxy of the future path-law, allowing for a deterministic evaluation of expected returns. This transition from stochastic branching to a single-pass linear evaluation significantly reduces computational complexity and variance. We prove that this framework preserves fundamental contraction properties and ensures stable generalisation even in the presence of heavy-tailed noise. Our results demonstrate that by grounding reinforcement learning in the topological features of path-space, agents can achieve proactive risk management and superior policy stability in highly volatile, continuous-time environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6357078\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0012363300003636\", \"title\": [\"Dynamic Path Planning for Autonomous Vehicles Using Adaptive Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0012363300003636\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6877184\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Negotiation via Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents: Efficiency, Fairness, and Mechanisms\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Business-to-business (B2B) markets power the global economy, yet complex bilateral negotiations often remain slow, fragmented, and inefficient when parties must bargain over multiple issues under private information. Existing market mechanisms rarely solve this tension among efficiency, agility, and privacy. We address this challenge by designing and evaluating an agent-to-agent negotiation framework for multi-issue bilateral exchange. In our setting, autonomous buyer and seller agents hold heterogeneous private preferences and learn adaptive bargaining strategies through self-play reinforcement learning under two-sided incomplete information. The result is striking: near-efficient and fair agreements emerge from decentralized, self-interested interactions without requiring either party to reveal private preferences to the counterparty or a central platform. Across heterogeneous negotiation environments, the agents capture about 91% of the socially optimal surplus in complex multi-issue settings and up to 98% in canonical single-issue benchmarks. We identify two mechanisms behind this performance: interepisode convergence toward reciprocal bargaining strategies and intra-episode inference that helps agents resolve late-stage impasses. We also uncover a counterintuitive boundary condition: payoff observability can undermine, rather than facilitate, cooperation. These findings suggest a core design principle for agentic commerce: privacy preservation and economic efficiency can be complements, not tradeoffs.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6877184\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4337/9781848449268.00008\", \"title\": [\"Path Dependence versus Path-breaking Crises: An Alternative View\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4337/9781848449268.00008\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2009, 7, 30]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "daa887d6355c09a9e73aa1cf3bcebdec4416aaf892a15b12053cf772561c3d67", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "divergent_values", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6357078", "doi:10.5220/0012363300003636", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6877184", "doi:10.4337/9781848449268.00008"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6357078", "https://doi.org/10.5220/0012363300003636", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6877184", "https://doi.org/10.4337/9781848449268.00008"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
